Vacuum flywheel: What Claude proposes to reach at least 99 %.

A 20 cm, 12 kg steel disc inside a vacuum chamber, floating on two stronger magnetic bearings (at each end, 16 magnets on the axle inside 24 fixed ones), pushed up to 3,000 rpm. Nothing touches it except a needle tip that holds it along the axle, and there is no air to slow it down.

It keeps almost all the energy you give it: after 10 minutes it still has 99.88 %, after an hour 99.3 %, and it takes almost an hour and a half to drop below 99 %. The only loss is the needle rubbing, and since it carries so much energy (3,035 J) that rubbing hardly shows. But it does not create energy: it loses a little every second and, if you take electricity out, it slows down too. It is as close to perpetual motion as you can get: storing very well, never creating.
